cards.card_text: She says, “God has vindicated me; He has heard my plea and given me a son.”
cards.verse_text: Then Rachel said, “God has vindicated me; He has heard my plea and given me a son.” So she named him Dan.

cards.card_text: Then the song turns toward hope: the LORD will vindicate His people.
cards.verse_text: In due time their foot will slip; for their day of disaster is near, and their doom is coming quickly.” For the LORD will vindicate His people and have compassion on His servants when He sees that their strength is gone and no one remains, slave or free.

cards.card_text: David says, "The LORD judges the peoples…" Then he asks the LORD to vindicate him.
cards.verse_text: The LORD judges the peoples; vindicate me, O LORD, according to my righteousness and integrity.
cards.snippet: The LORD judges the peoples; vindicate me, O LORD, according to my righteousness and integrity.

cards.card_text: The psalmist says God will incline His ear to vindicate the fatherless and oppressed, so the men of the earth may strike terror no more.
cards.verse_text: You will incline Your ear, to vindicate the fatherless and oppressed, that the men of the earth may strike terror no more.

cards.card_text: He opens with, "Vindicate me, O LORD!"
David asks the LORD to vindicate him.

cards.verse_text: Vindicate me by Your righteousness, O LORD my God, and do not let them gloat over me.

cards.card_text: Its writer asks God to vindicate him and plead his case against an ungodly nation.
cards.verse_text: Vindicate me, O God, and plead my case against an ungodly nation; deliver me from deceitful and unjust men.
cards.snippet: Vindicate me, O God, and plead my case against an ungodly nation; deliver…

cards.card_text: Next the prayer asks for the king to vindicate the afflicted among the people.
cards.verse_text: May he vindicate the afflicted among the people; may he save the children of the needy and crush the oppressor.

cards.card_text: The psalm says the LORD will vindicate His people and will have ___ on His servants.
cards.verse_text: For the LORD will vindicate His people and will have compassion on His servants.
cards.snippet: For the LORD will vindicate His people and will have compassion on His servants.

cards.card_text: He says, "State your case, so that you may be vindicated." Then the LORD brings up Israel's first father and their spokesmen.
cards.verse_text: State your case, so that you may be vindicated.
cards.snippet: State your case, so that you may be vindicated.

cards.card_text: The speaker asks, "Who will dare to contend with Me?" Right before that, what does He say about the One who vindicates Him?
cards.verse_text: The One who vindicates Me is near.
cards.snippet: The One who vindicates Me is near.

cards.card_text: Right after saying the LORD has seen the wrong done to him, the writer asks the LORD to vindicate his cause.
cards.verse_text: You have seen, O LORD, the wrong done to me; vindicate my cause!
cards.snippet: You have seen, O LORD, the wrong done to me; vindicate my cause!

cards.card_text: They say, "Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!" And Jesus ends with this: "But wisdom is vindicated by her actions."
cards.verse_text: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is vindicated by her actions.”
cards.snippet: …and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is vindicated by her actions.”

cards.card_text: He says the mystery of godliness is great, and he lays it out line by line: "He appeared in the flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, was seen by angels…"
cards.verse_text: By common confession, the mystery of godliness is great: He appeared in the flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, was seen by angels, was proclaimed among the nations, was believed in throughout the world, was taken up in glory.
